profile.subseg: Power Cables; Telecom Optical Fiber Cables; Railway Signaling Cables; House Wires; Special Cables
profile.themes: US Export Growth; Debt-Free Status; Greenfield Capacity Expansion

bull_bear.body: Debt repayment completed (zero net debt); surplus cash directed to Narmadapuram Greenfield capex (Rs.150cr Phase-1); no dividend or buyback mentioned; future allocation to capex and working capital efficiency
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: US tariff volatility (current duty: 14%-15%, potential reciprocal duties post-July 8); metal price volatility; execution risk at new plant; over-reliance on US market (95% of exports); working capital discipline may constrain growth if domestic demand surges
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, pragmatic, and outcome-focused; CEO prioritizes absolute rupee profit over margin percentages; dismisses ‘new normal’ margin narratives; emphasizes flexibility, volume-driven growth, and shareholder returns; acknowledges tariff risks but expresses confidence in market position and customer loyalty
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite 57% metal volume growth, revenue grew only 47% — indicating commodity price deflation, not product mix shift; working capital reduction from 155 to 101 days was achieved by reducing exposure to slow-paying government clients; export order book is deliberately kept lean (~50% of total) to preserve capacity flexibility for higher-margin opportunities
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Debt/Equity improved from 0.87x (FY22) to 0.15x (FY26), with net worth growing from Rs 202 Cr to Rs 778 Cr over the same period.
- Working capital days stood at 96 in Q1 FY27, down from 101 days in Q4 FY26.
- FY27 roadmap prioritises restoring profitability toward pre-tariff margins as export markets normalise, alongside continued investment in the Narmadapuram expansion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Power Cables: 50% of FY25 revenue (Rs.787cr, +77% YoY); Domestic: Rs.1,093cr (38% YoY); Export: Rs.483cr (75% YoY, 95% to US); House Wires: Rs.26cr in Q4; Railway: Rs.18cr in Q4; Telecom: minor share
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- 70+ years of domain experience across power, railways, telecom, renewables, domestic wires and EPC/turnkey, with 950+ institutional clients carrying deep government/infrastructure exposure.
- Largest Indian LV (up to 600V) cable exporter to the US in CY2025, with presence across 35+ export geographies and 8 active US distributors (up from 2 in FY22).
- Capacity optionality via the Narmadapuram greenfield facility opens the next leg in EHV cables, specialised transmission conductors, E-Beam and other specialised cables.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [US tariff shock] An August 2025 US tariff shock drove a sharp swing in channel mix: export share fell from 43% in H1 FY26 to 16% in H2 FY26 (domestic pivot to 84%), before recovering to 29% export share in Q1 FY27 as tariff uncertainty eased.
- [Market data] Market capitalisation Rs 2,103 Cr; 52-week high/low Rs 75.4 / Rs 28.4; shares outstanding 30,52,09,814, as of 30 June 2026.
- [Shareholding, June 2026] Promoter 49.2%, Public 50.2%, FPI 0.5%, DII 0.1%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin down to 8.5% in FY25 from 9% due to lower realized prices from falling copper/aluminum commodity costs (metal price decline offset volume growth); Q4 margin dipped to 6.6% due to strategic volume ramp-up and tariff transition costs in US; cost structure remains leveraged to metal input, but working capital efficiency offsets pressure
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 30% CAGR over next 5 years; margin: no fixed target, focus on absolute profit; order inflow: no specific guidance, but order book maintained at Rs.650cr; capex/commissioning: Rs.150cr Phase-1 capex at Narmadapuram, commercial production targeted by end-FY26
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.650cr as of March 31, 2025 (Rs.328cr domestic; Rs.325cr export); export orders constitute ~50% of order book, primarily US-bound
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: US export market penetration (target: 40% of revenue); Narmadapuram Greenfield plant (Phase-1: Rs.150cr capex, targeting Rs.1,000cr revenue in 3 years); potential entry into 20kV cables; scaling domestic government and private infrastructure demand
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Paramount achieved record revenue of Rs.1,587cr in FY25 with 47% YoY growth, driven by 75% export surge to the US and 57% metal volume growth, while becoming debt-free and reducing working capital days from 155 to 101; the key matter is the Rs.150cr Phase-1 capex at Narmadapuram plant targeting Rs.1,000cr revenue in 3 years, which will unlock scalable, high-margin capacity beyond existing plants.
